jobs.title: Director of Corporate and Financial Services (CFO/Treasurer)
jobs.description:
Located within the traditional land of the Anishnaabek, Haudenosaunee and Wendat—Wyandot-Wyandotte peoples, the Town of The Blue Mountains is a four-season community with stunning natural features, including the Niagara Escarpment, Beaver Valley and the Georgian Bay shoreline. Internationally recognized as a four-season tourism destination, The Blue Mountains offers a high-quality lifestyle that caters to families looking to build a solid foundation, adventurers looking to go off the beaten path and relaxation seekers taking in and experiencing the very best the area has to offer.

The Town is looking for people with a shared commitment to building a sustainable community, as well as shared values of Accountability & Transparency, Leadership, Stewardship, Respect and Collaboration.

With a combined operational and capital budget of approximately $55M and over 170 permanent, part-time and seasonal staff, our municipality is committed to meeting the needs of our residents and business community by delivering efficient and effective services.

Come gain a unique experience in the 2nd fastest-growing municipality in Canada!

Inspire our Future

As the new Director of Corporate and Financial Services
, you are an insightful and proven strategic advisor to elected officials with a view to both short and long-term planning and financial sustainability. In addition, you have an ability to lead and support effective operations through the development and management of policies, procedures and programs, while leading the team activity related to finance, purchasing, risk management, fleet and facilities and information technology.

Reporting directly to the Chief Administrative Officer, you will be key member of the Senior Leadership Team and provide inspired and collaborative leadership, vision, direction as well as specialized advice, consultation to staff across the organization while ensuring the Town’s financial resources are optimally utilized in the achieving the operational and strategic goals and objectives of the municipality.

In your capacity as Director
of Corporate and Financial Services
you will provide financial advice to Council, the CAO and the Senior Leadership Team while managing the service areas within financial planning, accounting, purchasing, risk management, fleet and facilities and information technology. This will include directing and managing staff, preparation and maintenance of the budget, ensuring adequacy of financial controls and that general government operations are carried out in a cost efficient, effective and customer centric manner, and that all statutory and regulatory obligations are met.

Ideal Qualifications:

Education and Designations:
a University degree relative to area of responsibility (accounting/commerce/finance or business) plus a professional accounting designation (CPA).
Municipal Management experience:
10 or more years of progressively responsible relevant work experience with at least six years’ experience in a senior municipal financial management position, including experience working with elected officials/boards.
Finance and Corporate Services Experience:
Expert level knowledge/experience related to budget planning, accounting, internal controls, financial reporting, development charges, taxation, capital planning/asset management, purchasing, risk management and information technology in a municipal setting.
Strategic Acumen:
Ability to think and act strategically in a political and community service environment with a solid understanding of various types of strategic and planning processes required to develop appropriate corporate and departmental short/long term goals and objectives.

Critical Thinking:
Analytical, problem solving and decision-making skills to enable the assessment of multiple issues, the development of options and implementation of decisions necessary for the effective and efficient operation of the department recognizing impacts and mitigating repercussions.
People Leadership:
Exceptional leadership skills with proven ability to build, lead, and mentor a strong and enthusiastic staff teams and external alliances/partnerships.
Legislation:
Demonstrated knowledge of Municipal, Provincial, Federal legislation, regulations, and guidelines including municipal government operations, principles, best practices, and processes.
Technical Acumen:
Advanced technical literacy with the Microsoft suite of products, the internet and proficiency in a range of other computer software applications related to finance, payroll and other corporate productivity software ideally in a municipal setting.
Communication:
Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication, presentation, facilitation and negotiation skills.

Why join the Town of The Blue Mountains

If you like scenic vistas, the outdoors, fresh air, and attainable housing then the Town of The Blue Mountain is the place to be for an unmatched quality of life, benefits include:
Modern Office Environment
- modern offices with no fee parking.
Employee Development
- staff leadership and professional development training opportunities.
Housing
– Blue Mountain provides many opportunities for a robust lifestyle. The choices range from developed urban centres in nearby communities, to a range of rural properties to waterfront. The most important point is that prices are less than less than the GTA, unless you are considering waterfront.
Education
- An exceptional educational system at both the elementary and secondary levels.
Healthcare
– Access to an excellent community hospitals in nearby Collingwood and Meaford.
Outdoor Lifestyle
- Access to a range of outdoor activities. If you like exploring, boating, fishing, hiking, golf, x-country/ downhill skiing or snowmobiling, this is the place to be.
Compensation and Benefits
- a very competitive salary ranging from $155,931.98 - $182,436.05, plus a comprehensive benefits package and OMERS pension.

How to Apply

To explore this opportunity please apply via email with your resume and covering letter as soon as possible to careers@waterhousesearch.net
quoting
project TBM-DCFS
.

Should you wish to speak to our Executive Recruiter or to receive a detailed position description please contact Amy Oliveira at 416-705-424-5944, amy@waterhousesearch.net
or Jon Stungevicius at 416-214-9233, jon@waterhousesearch.net
.

We appreciate all applications, however, only those candidates invited for an interview will be acknowledged. Personal information contained in your resume is collected under the authority of the Municipal Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act and will be used strictly for employment assessment purposes. The Town of the Blue Mountain is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity in the workplace.

jobs.title: Vice President Finance
jobs.description:
VICE PRESIDENT, FINANCE AND ACCOUNTING

Toronto | Hybrid

Are you a finance leader who enjoys combining the rigour of public company reporting with the pace and variety of an entrepreneurial business?

Our client, a growing publicly traded consumer products company with manufacturing operations and an expanding international presence, is seeking a Vice President, Finance and Accounting to lead its core finance functions and work closely with the CFO on the next stage of the organization’s development.

This opportunity offers broad responsibility, direct exposure to executive leadership and the Audit Committee, and the ability to influence how finance supports an increasingly complex business. You’ll lead an established team, strengthen financial processes and contribute to financing, acquisitions and other significant business initiatives.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Reporting to the CFO, you will oversee accounting, financial reporting, controllership, treasury, tax and internal controls. You will combine sound technical judgment with practical business advice, helping senior leaders understand financial results, evaluate risks and make informed decisions.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Lead quarterly and annual financial reporting, including financial statements, MD&A and other public company reporting requirements.
• Oversee monthly, quarterly and annual close processes, improving accuracy, efficiency and accountability.
• Guide the assessment of complex accounting matters, including acquisitions, valuations, impairment and financial instruments.
• Manage external auditor relationships and lead annual audits and quarterly reviews.
• Strengthen the internal control environment, including SOX/ICFR compliance and continuous improvement.
• Oversee treasury, banking relationships, credit facilities, covenant compliance and foreign exchange exposure.
• Improve cash forecasting and working capital visibility across inventory, receivables and payables.
• Provide leadership over operational accounting, including inventory, standard costing and manufacturing variances.
• Oversee tax compliance and planning in partnership with external advisors.
• Support the CFO on financing, M&A, financial analysis and other strategic initiatives.
• Present financial results and significant accounting matters to executive leadership and the Audit Committee.
• Lead and develop the finance team while advancing process improvements, shared services and more effective use of systems.

WHAT YOU BRING

You are a CPA with public company finance leadership experience and the judgment to connect technical accounting issues to their business implications. You understand the detail behind the numbers, know when to ask further questions and can communicate your conclusions clearly and confidently.

Your background includes:

• Significant progressive experience in accounting and finance leadership within a public company environment.
• Strong knowledge of IFRS, external financial reporting and public company requirements.
• Experience leading audits and managing relationships with major accounting firms.
• A strong understanding of SOX/ICFR and experience improving financial controls.
• Experience with treasury, cash management, debt facilities and corporate tax matters.
• Proven ability to lead and develop finance teams and build productive relationships across functions.
• Experience presenting to senior executives, Boards or Audit Committees.
• The commercial judgment to support acquisitions, financing and other significant business decisions.
• A record of improving finance processes, systems and reporting.

Manufacturing, consumer products or comparable operational experience would be particularly valuable, especially an understanding of inventory, costing and margin drivers. Experience supporting M&A and integration would also be an asset.

Just as important is how you work. You build trust, take ownership and remain effective as priorities change. You are comfortable moving between executive discussions and detailed problem-solving, and you bring a collaborative approach to supporting colleagues and developing your team.

WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE APPEALING

• A broad finance leadership mandate and a close working relationship with the CFO.
• Direct exposure to executive leadership and the Audit Committee.
• Opportunities to contribute to acquisitions, financing and business growth.
• A meaningful improvement agenda spanning cash forecasting, shared services and finance processes.
• A collaborative, respectful environment that values initiative and sound judgment.
• A hybrid work arrangement and a compensation package that includes annual incentives, long-term equity and retirement savings matching.

To learn more, please contact me directly or send your résumé through LinkedIn. All inquiries will be treated confidentially.

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

jobs.title: Director, AI Solutions Strategy & Planning
jobs.description:
We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Why this role is on the menu

Instacart is building a new, distinctive pillar of the Instacart Platform — an emerging portfolio of AI-driven retailer solutions — and the go-to-market infrastructure to scale it is being built right now. The opportunity is real, but translating it into scalable commercialization frameworks, pricing strategies, and GTM plans requires specialized expertise and a dedicated strategy and planning leader. We're hiring a Director of AI Solutions Strategy & Planning to lead that work end-to-end. This role sits at the intersection of enterprise strategy and frontier AI, working cross-functionally with Product, Sales, Marketing, Legal, and Customer Success to shape how Instacart becomes the preferred technology partner for grocery retailers.

What You'll Cook Up In Your First Year

A comprehensive GTM strategy for Instacart's AI-driven solutions is defined and in motion — spanning consumer experiences, ecommerce analytics, and enhanced retailer workflows — with clear positioning, pricing frameworks, and retailer onboarding playbooks in place.
Cross-functional alignment across Product, Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Legal is established, with governance forums running smoothly and transparent decision-making processes embedded across GTM and product teams.
Pilot programs and experimentation frameworks are launched and producing real impact — validating AI-powered products with real retailer feedback and iterating based on measurable performance metrics.
Sales teams are enabled and equipped with AI-specific strategies, enablement materials, and training programs that accelerate adoption and pipeline velocity.
Market intelligence and competitive analysis are regularly informing product and commercialization decisions, keeping Instacart's AI solutions competitive, scalable, and aligned with evolving retailer needs.

The secret ingredients we're looking for

Must-have Pantry Staples (Minimum Qualifications)

8+ years of experience in strategy, product commercialization, or GTM planning, with a proven track record of defining and executing strategies for emerging offerings and driving measurable market impact.
Experience developing GTM strategies for AI-powered products, retailer solutions, or enterprise technology platforms.
Deep understanding of AI technologies, with the ability to translate technical concepts into business value for diverse audiences.
Expertise in product positioning, pricing frameworks, and solution packaging.
Strong analytical capabilities, including experience with modeling, forecasting, and evaluating solution performance.
Exceptional cross-functional leadership skills with a track record of influencing stakeholders across Product, Sales, Marketing, Legal, and Finance.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills for simplifying complex concepts and presenting to internal and external audiences.
Strong quantitative skills to help inform opportunity sizing, impact assessment, pricing strategy, and financial outlook in partnership with cross-functional peers.
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in ambiguous and rapidly changing environments, with a focus on iterative learning and innovation.

Optional Garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)

Familiarity with conversational AI, ecommerce analytics, or retail technology applications.
Advanced knowledge of AI product monetization models, including subscription, usage-based, and value-based models.
MBA or advanced degree in business, technology, or a related field.

Instacart provides highly market-competitive compensation and benefits in each location where our employees work. This role is remote and the base pay range for a successful candidate is dependent on their permanent work location. Please review our Flex First remote work policy here. Currently, we are only hiring in the following provinces: Ontario, Alberta, British Columbia, and Nova Scotia.

Offers may vary based on many factors, such as candidate experience and skills required for the role. Additionally, this role is eligible for a new hire equity grant as well as annual refresh grants. Please read more about our benefits offerings here.

jobs.title: Director, Global Technology & Operations Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
The Director, Global Technology & Operations Strategy & Transformation will help shape and execute strategic priorities across Global Technology & Operations (GTO), with a significant focus on leading the AI program and translating strategy into measurable business outcomes.

The Director will lead the AI program across GTO, bringing together strategy, business case development, funding, program governance, technical delivery, adoption, and value realization. This includes managing AI program funding, ensuring funding is directed to the appropriate initiatives and teams, and maintaining visibility into how initiatives are progressing against delivery commitments, defined success criteria, and approved budgets.

Working closely with the VP of GTO and senior stakeholders across Business, Technology, Enterprise AI, Finance, and Risk, the Director will provide an integrated view of the AI program, drive accountability across teams, identify areas requiring leadership attention, and enable informed decisions on priorities, funding, execution, and outcomes.

The Director will also help shape how GTO delivers its AI agenda, establishing approaches to prioritize and sequence initiatives, accelerate execution, and scale reusable AI capabilities across segments and countries. This includes helping establish a practical path from opportunity identification through development, production, and adoption, while focusing resources on initiatives that can deliver the greatest strategic and business impact.

Position Responsibilities

GTO Strategy & Transformation: Partner with the VP of GTO and senior leaders to translate strategic priorities into executable strategies, roadmaps, initiatives, and measurable outcomes. Connect priorities across teams, identify opportunities and risks, and provide insights and recommendations to support executive decision-making.
AI Program Leadership & Governance: Lead the end-to-end AI and Automation program across GTO, establishing a single integrated view of initiatives, priorities, dependencies, funding, and outcomes. Establish program governance and operating rhythms and work across Product Owners, Segment Leads, Technology, and business and functional partners to drive execution, alignment, and accountability.
AI Strategy, Prioritization & Delivery Approach: Help define how GTO identifies, assesses, prioritizes, sequences, and delivers AI initiatives. Develop practical prioritization and delivery approaches that consider strategic alignment, business value, delivery readiness, scalability, complexity, funding requirements, dependencies, and risk. Continuously assess the portfolio to ensure resources remain focused on the highest-value opportunities and identify where initiatives should be accelerated, repositioned, or deprioritized.
Business Case & AI Program Funding: Lead the planning, mobilization, and partner engagement required to develop business cases for AI execution and future funding, including cost-benefit analysis, expected outcomes, success criteria, delivery requirements, and risk considerations. Manage AI program funding and recommend allocation or reallocation across initiatives and teams based on strategic priorities, expected value, delivery readiness, and performance.
Delivery Excellence, Performance & Value Realization: Oversee AI initiatives across technical delivery, business outcomes, adoption, success criteria, budget utilization, risks, and dependencies. Assess whether initiatives are delivering against their original commitments, drive accountability for results, and identify where intervention, reprioritization, or funding adjustments are required. Ensure realized outcomes can be traced back to approved business cases and defined success measures.
Executive Reporting & Stakeholder Management: Provide the VP of GTO and senior leadership with a consolidated view of the AI program, including roadmap progress, funding utilization, delivery performance, value realization, risks, dependencies, and decisions required. Maintain effective engagement across sponsors, segments, Technology, Enterprise AI, Finance, Risk, and other partners, translating complex information into clear executive insights and recommendations.
AI-Driven Transformation & Reusable Capabilities: Identify opportunities to fundamentally redesign processes and ways of working through AI and Automation, moving beyond incremental improvements. Drive the development, reuse, and adoption of scalable AI capabilities, standards, playbooks, and common approaches that accelerate delivery and reduce duplication across GTO.

Required Qualifications

8+ years of experience across strategy and transformation, technology, AI, program management, product management, or related disciplines, with demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional programs.
Demonstrated experience leading large-scale AI, Automation, technology, innovation, or transformation programs, including program governance, prioritization, funding, delivery oversight, and performance management.
Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, with demonstrated experience translating strategy into prioritized programs, roadmaps, business cases, funding recommendations, and measurable outcomes.
Strong financial acumen, including experience developing and evaluating business cases, cost-benefit analysis, managing budgets and funding, establishing success measures, and assessing value realization.
Strong understanding of AI platforms and modern AI solution patterns, with sufficient technical fluency to understand delivery plans, challenge assumptions, assess dependencies and risks, and engage credibly with Technology and AI leaders.
Strong program leadership capabilities, including the ability to oversee multiple concurrent initiatives, establish governance and delivery frameworks, manage complex dependencies, and drive disciplined execution across Business and Technology teams.
Exceptional executive communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to synthesize complex strategic, financial, business, and technical information into clear insights, recommendations, and decisions for senior leadership.
Demonstrated ability to influence and challenge senior stakeholders, drive accountability without direct authority, create structure in ambiguous environments, and manage competing strategic priorities.
Demonstrated use of AI productivity tools and agentic workflows to accelerate analysis, synthesis, reporting, decision-making, and content development.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading or managing an enterprise-scale AI, Automation, technology, innovation, or transformation program, including prioritization, funding, delivery, and value realization.
Experience establishing program governance, portfolio prioritization frameworks, business cases, executive reporting, and value-realization models.
Familiarity with enterprise AI architecture, MLOps/LLMOps, AI evaluation, Responsible AI, model governance, and the considerations involved in moving AI solutions from development into production.
Experience scaling reusable AI capabilities across multiple teams, business segments, or geographies.
Experience partnering directly with senior executives on strategy, funding, program performance, prioritization, and enterprise transformation.
Financial services or other highly regulated industry experience strongly preferred.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

jobs.description:
Position Title:

Director of Digital Products, Ad Experiences and Audience Activation (Hybrid/Telework)

Status of Employment:

Permanent

Position Language Requirement:

English, French

Language Skills:

English (Reading - C - Advanced), English (Speaking - C - Advanced), English (Writing - B - Intermediate), French (Reading - C - Advanced), French (Speaking - C - Advanced), French (Writing - B - Intermediate)

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance.

Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

2026-11-01 11:59 PM

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

Job Overview:

This position is part of the Digital Media department, which oversees CBC and Radio-Canada’s flagship digital products.

In partnership with the Media Solutions division, the person in this role plays a key role in shaping the vision for CBC-RC monetization experience evolution. They leverage a deep understanding of digital, user behaviours, market trends, and technology to inform strategic thinking and guide product direction. They also will support the day to day audience segmentation activities and support and inform the monetization data strategy and roadmaps.

They lead the monetization products evolution — from testing to discovery to delivery — balancing user needs with business objectives. They work to enhance the overall experience and drive innovation to retain current clients, audiences and attract new ones. They also ensure the continuous evolution of tools and solutions that support Media Solutions and Marketing team operations as it relates to audience segmentation.

They collaborate with product managers to coordinate the work carried out by the product teams. They maintain strong ties with the sales, marketing, communications, and ad tech teams to ensure strategic and operational alignment.

This role also aims to create synergies across products to strengthen engagement within Radio-Canada’s broader digital ecosystem. The individual actively contributes to the organization’s digital transformation initiatives.

Why this role is important:

You are responsible for leading and evolving the organizations ability to drive revenue through the creation and maintenance of innovative ad products and services.
You are responsible for developing a strategic roadmap that aligns to the strategic priorities of the Media Solutions (Sales) team, by identifying and executing on the highest priorities.
You enable the evolution of ad formats, the integration of technologies within the ad tech stack, the evolution of the data strategy and the enablement of key features and improvements for our users.
You establish a testing practice that is continuously finding ways to improve the existing ad experience with new ad loads, scenarios by user type and ad formats to adopt.

jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. Conditions and Compensation Lacroix Medical Group offers a competitive total compensation package including: Annual salary of $140,000 to $175,000, depending on experience and expertise; 4 weeks of vacation and 4 paid personal days; RRSP+ program with employer contribution; Cell phone allowance; Lacroix Health Credit; and an annual Lacroix gift card. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Business travel expense account for trips outside your usual work area

Join a growing network and become a key player in the future of private medicine in Quebec.

Apply now and make a real difference.

The Director, Global Technology & Operations Strategy & Transformation will help shape and execute strategic priorities across Global Technology & Operations (GTO), with a significant focus on leading the AI program and translating strategy into measurable business outcomes.

The Director will lead the AI program across GTO, bringing together strategy, business case development, funding, program governance, technical delivery, adoption, and value realization. This includes managing AI program funding, ensuring funding is directed to the appropriate initiatives and teams, and maintaining visibility into how initiatives are progressing against delivery commitments, defined success criteria, and approved budgets.

Working closely with the VP of GTO and senior stakeholders across Business, Technology, Enterprise AI, Finance, and Risk, the Director will provide an integrated view of the AI program, drive accountability across teams, identify areas requiring leadership attention, and enable informed decisions on priorities, funding, execution, and outcomes.

The Director will also help shape how GTO delivers its AI agenda, establishing approaches to prioritize and sequence initiatives, accelerate execution, and scale reusable AI capabilities across segments and countries. This includes helping establish a practical path from opportunity identification through development, production, and adoption, while focusing resources on initiatives that can deliver the greatest strategic and business impact.

Position Responsibilities

GTO Strategy & Transformation: Partner with the VP of GTO and senior leaders to translate strategic priorities into executable strategies, roadmaps, initiatives, and measurable outcomes. Connect priorities across teams, identify opportunities and risks, and provide insights and recommendations to support executive decision-making.
AI Program Leadership & Governance: Lead the end-to-end AI and Automation program across GTO, establishing a single integrated view of initiatives, priorities, dependencies, funding, and outcomes. Establish program governance and operating rhythms and work across Product Owners, Segment Leads, Technology, and business and functional partners to drive execution, alignment, and accountability.
AI Strategy, Prioritization & Delivery Approach: Help define how GTO identifies, assesses, prioritizes, sequences, and delivers AI initiatives. Develop practical prioritization and delivery approaches that consider strategic alignment, business value, delivery readiness, scalability, complexity, funding requirements, dependencies, and risk. Drive the development, reuse, and adoption of scalable AI capabilities, standards, playbooks, and common approaches that accelerate delivery and reduce duplication across GTO.

8+ years of experience across strategy and transformation, technology, AI, program management, product management, or related disciplines, with demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional programs.

Exceptional executive communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to synthesize complex strategic, financial, business, and technical information into clear insights, recommendations, and decisions for senior leadership.
Demonstrated ability to influence and challenge senior stakeholders, drive accountability without direct authority, create structure in ambiguous environments, and manage competing strategic priorities.
Demonstrated use of AI productivity tools and agentic workflows to accelerate analysis, synthesis, reporting, decision-making, and content development.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading or managing an enterprise-scale AI, Automation, technology, innovation, or transformation program, including prioritization, funding, delivery, and value realization.
Experience establishing program governance, portfolio prioritization frameworks, business cases, executive reporting, and value-realization models.

new_jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group
comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

Since its founding in 2009, the Lacroix Medical Group has experienced sustained growth and now has nearly 350 employees across its various divisions. Driven by an ambitious and entrepreneurial vision, the organization continues its expansion across the province and aspires to accelerate its development in national and international markets.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation

Mandate

Reporting to the Director of Marketing, the Digital Performance Manager
plays a key role in the growth, reach, and success of the Lacroix Medical Group.

Passionate about digital marketing, data, and innovation, this individual leverages their expertise to develop high-performing strategies that generate a tangible impact on our business objectives. Their daily challenge: transforming data into opportunities, strategies into results, and ideas into measurable actions. In a dynamic environment encompassing multiple clinics, services, and business lines, the successful candidate will lead the organization's overall digital performance. They will develop, deploy, measure, and optimize digital media campaigns to increase our visibility, generate business opportunities, and maximize the return on our marketing investments. A true strategic partner to internal teams, this proactive individual will work closely with various stakeholders to understand their challenges, identify the best growth opportunities, and recommend innovative, results-oriented solutions. Thanks to her expertise, she actively contributes to the evolution of our digital maturity, the continuous improvement of our practices, and the achievement of our growth ambitions. Curious, analytical, and always on the lookout for new trends, the Digital Performance Manager enjoys experimenting, innovating, and pushing boundaries. Whether through campaign optimization, advanced data analytics, artificial intelligence, geolocation, or new approaches to digital marketing, this individual helps maintain the Lacroix Medical Group's position among the most innovative organizations in its sector. If you are performance-driven, thrive on challenges, and want to grow in an environment where your ideas will have a concrete and measurable impact, this position is for you. Your Role Take charge of the activation, management, and analysis of digital media campaigns (SEM, programmatic, and social media). Ensure the implementation of trafficking, online deployment, execution, daily bid monitoring, campaign health, and performance analysis. Manage and ensure adherence to media budgets while optimizing ROI. investments. Support internal clients, understand their needs, advise them, and recommend the best digital strategies. Ensure rigorous monitoring of conversions, data quality, and overall campaign performance. In-depth analysis of results, identify optimization opportunities, and share learnings with team members. Effectively navigate between multiple projects, brands, and priorities simultaneously. Manage and optimize Google Ads and Meta Ads campaigns to achieve established performance objectives. Utilize measurement and optimization tools such as Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console, and SEMrush. Design, maintain, and analyze performance dashboards in Looker Studio. Constantly monitor best practices in Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Search Engine Optimization (SEO). Participate to the development, implementation, and execution of digital strategies with the team's various experts. Identify and recommend new acquisition, conversion, and optimization opportunities to support the organization's growth.

The Ideal Candidate

Bachelor's degree in marketing, communications, or a related field.
Minimum of 6 to 8 years of experience in digital marketing and performance campaign management.
Experience in an environment encompassing multiple divisions, brands, or business lines.
Agency experience (a significant asset).
Valid Google Ads certification.
Excellent command of Google Ads, Meta Ads, Google Analytics 4, and Looker Studio.
Experience with other platforms and tools, including Google Tag Manager and TikTok Ads Manager.
Strong analytical skills and a strong results orientation.
Highly autonomous, rigorous, and organized.
Initiative and ability to thrive in a constantly evolving environment.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a context of rapid growth.
Excellent command of both spoken and written French and English.
Strong interest in innovation, artificial intelligence, and the evolution of digital technologies.

Our Benefits

Lacroix Gift Card of $500 per year, including fast access to a doctor.
Annual Health Account of $1,100, which can reach $2,000 based on years of service. FTQ Workers' Fund with employer contribution. Annual budget dedicated to continuing education. Real opportunities for career advancement and professional development. Three weeks of vacation upon hiring. Four paid floating holidays per year. Hybrid work model. Free parking. Modern, bright, and collaborative work environment. Unlimited coffee and employee lounge. Join an ambitious, growing organization where your expertise, ideas, and passion will directly contribute to shaping the future of private healthcare. Quebec.

new_jobs.title: Senior Director, Energy & Power, Corporate, Infrastructure and Project Finance Group - Toronto
new_jobs.description:
Senior Director, Energy and Power, Corporate, Infrastructure and Project Finance Group

Fitch Ratings’ Energy and Power, Corporate, Infrastructure and Project Finance
Group is currently seeking a Senior Director based out of our New York, Chicago, or Toronto office.

This role will report into the Head of Energy and Power, Corporate, Infrastructure and Project Finance Group for North America.

What We Offer

Fitch Ratings is seeking a senior credit analyst with 10+ years of solid project finance related experience in the infrastructure sector. The primary responsibilities of the successful candidate will be to focus on the analysis, execution and rating of infrastructure and project finance transactions, in particular those related to energy and power infrastructure assets in the US and Canada.

The ability to shape the strategic course for the infrastructure team.
Opportunity to take a leadership role analyzing some cutting-edge transactions.
Be part of a growing credit team in the ever-evolving infrastructure space.
A sector that is seeing significant investments resulting in a diversity of new and interesting credits on which to provide independent evaluations.
Experienced and collaborative team and opportunity to learn about wider infrastructure space.
Open culture where employees are able to exchange ideas and perspectives.

We’ll Count On You To

Work on leading ratings analysis, execution and research on new and existing North American transactions.
Evaluating innovative credit structures and participating in global criteria development.
Identifying relevant trends, assessing their credit impact and highlighting these trends in updated industry and market focused reports/presentations.
Gathering and analyzing quantitative and qualitative data and legal documents for the purpose of producing ratings, publishing credit reports, and contributing to special research reports.
Maintain a strong external network and profile that continues to build Fitch's reputation for analytical excellence by representing Fitch in a compelling and persuasive manner at industry conferences, webinars, issuer meetings/site visits and through media communication.
Develop and grow strong relationships with the other analytical groups at Fitch to ensure analytical consistency and efficient execution of transactions that involve multiple groups.
Mentor junior members of the Energy and Power Infrastructure team.

What You Need To Have

10+ years of solid project finance related experience in energy and power infrastructure including development of credit or underwriting approach.
Proven project finance and infrastructure credit skills gained in a bank credit department, a rating agency, buy side credit department, etc.
Solid writing and verbal communication skills.
An open mind to think expansively about the opportunity and risk in the evolving infrastructure landscape.
Excellent modelling skills and thorough familiarity with spreadsheet-based financial models.
Ability to read and fully comprehend complex structures and to ask probing questions to issuers and their advisers.
Demonstrated ability to lead and handle multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to work to tight deadlines and display a strong degree of flexibility to take on additional responsibilities, as required.
Employee management experience.

What Would Make You Stand Out

Rating agency experience.
Ratings advisory work.
A deep understanding of and a keen interest in infrastructure and project finance.
A professional background in capital markets and/or credit analysis.
Experience in interpreting complex legal documents such as bank agreements and bond indentures.
A strong pattern of leadership and the ability to proactively and successfully interact with various stakeholders, both within and outside of the organization.
CFA.
Master’s degree in Finance, Business or Public Administration preferred.

Why Fitch?

At Fitch Group, the combined power of our global perspectives is what differentiates us. Our global network of colleagues comes together to accomplish things greater than they ever could alone.

Every team member is essential to our business and each perspective is critical to our success. We embrace a diverse culture that encourages a free exchange of ideas, guaranteeing your voice will be heard and your work will have an impact, regardless of seniority.

We are building incredible things at Fitch and we invite you to join us on our journey.

Fitch Ratings is a leading provider of credit ratings, commentary and research. Dedicated to providing value beyond the rating through independent and prospective credit opinions, Fitch ratings offers global perspectives shaped by strong local market experience and credit market expertise. The additional context, perspective and insights we provide have helped fund a century of growth and enables our clients to make important credit judgements with confidence.

Fitch Group is a global leader in financial information services with operations in more than 30 countries. Wholly owned by the Hearst Corporation, we are comprised of three main businesses: Fitch Ratings | Fitch Solutions |

Fitch Learning.

For More Information Please Visit Our Websites

www.fitchratings.com | www.fitchsolutions.com | www.fitchlearning.com

Fitch is committed to providing global securities markets with objective, timely, independent and forward-looking credit opinions. To protect Fitch’s credibility and reputation, our employees must take every precaution to avoid conflicts of interests or any appearance of a conflict of interest. Should you be successful in the recruitment process at Fitch Ratings you will be asked to declare any securities holdings and other potential conflicts prior to commencing employment. If you, or your immediate family, have any holdings that may conflict with your work responsibilities, you may be asked to divest yourself of them before beginning work.

Fitch Group is proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status, and other statuses protected by law.

FOR NEW YORK AND CHICAGO ROLES ONLY:
Expected base pay rates for the role will be between $190,000 and $225,000 per year. Actual salaries will be determined on an individualized basis and may vary based on factors including but not limited to education, training, experience, past performance, and other job-related factors. Base pay is one part of Fitch’s total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, discretionary bonuses, long-term incentives, and other benefits sponsored by Fitch.
